## Exit evidence

- Canonical 2026-07-28 core and every supported extension have requirement-level owners and passing negative controls.
- Legacy protocol support is explicit, bounded, telemetry-visible, and sunset-ready.
- Public SDK owns semantics and both real transports are thin tested adapters.
- Security, authorization, privacy, consent, caching, schema resource bounds, and observability gates pass.
- Tasks, skills, and Apps are negotiated extensions and absence preserves all core functionality.
- Packed and published npm, npx, bunx, stdio, and Streamable HTTP consumers pass the canonical agent journey.
- Source, contracts, generated schemas, docs, discovery, package metadata, release metadata, and runtime behavior agree exactly.
Outcome milestone: MCP 2026-07-28 interoperability proven from public SDK through released core and negotiated extensions
Declare the outcome reached only when current MCP behavior, compatibility, security, tasks, skills, Apps, transports, and released consumers pass one requirement-complete evidence gate.

The complete official requirement matrix has no unowned, untested, waived-without-expiry, or contradictory row; SDK, stdio, Streamable HTTP, tasks, skills, Apps, security, caching, and deprecation gates pass with proven negative controls; The exact released package and every advertised consumer surface report and execute the same protocol and extension contract; No critical or high MCP security, conformance, drift, release, or compatibility blocker remains open; The milestone evidence cites exact commit, package version, release, workflow runs, test commands, and immutable pm receipts
Graduate the MCP programme only after interoperable behavior and optional extensions are proven across SDK, transports, packages, and releases
The roadmap distinguishes protocol claims from exact evidence that real hosts can consume
The MCP capability epic is living scope and the SDK-complete milestone does not independently certify current protocol interoperability
